meta.description: Anubis (Automatic Network User Based Interface System): a server-driven UI framework for Kotlin Multiplatform. Screens are described as JSON on a Ktor server and rendered natively with Compose, so layouts can change without an app release.

caseStudy.title: Anubis
caseStudy.lead: Anubis (Automatic Network User Based Interface System): a server-driven UI framework for Kotlin Multiplatform. Screens are described as JSON on a Ktor server and rendered natively with Compose, so layouts can change without an app release.

cards.heading: Anubis
cards.subheading: The best way to build mobile apps

brief.title: The idea
text: App teams often need to change a screen faster than an App Store release allows. Anubis moves the layout to the server: the app knows how to draw a set of components, and the server decides which ones to show and in what order.
Adding an object to the JSON adds a component to the screen.

contributions.title: What I did
items: Worked on the shared models for the components: card, container, divider, text and text button.
Rendered the JSON object list natively with Compose Multiplatform, with images through Coil.
Worked with the Ktor client in the app and a Ktor server that serves the screens.
Built the sample Android and iOS apps and discussed the design with the team.

team.title: Team
team.text: Built by the internal mobile engineering team at Merkle, as internal reference work.

outcome.title: The result
outcome.text: A working reference for server-driven native UI, later included in the team's KMP Template.
